ethos.body1: Shamanic Travels is a private, selection-based journey across the high Andes and Amazonian basins. We do not provide group tours. We curate deep experiential thresholds for those ready to encounter Peru's living wisdom traditions.
ethos.body2: Combining the logistical precision of luxury travel with the profound silence of Peru's sacred geography, every element is managed with calm authority and absolute privacy.

journeys.meta: Each journey · 21 days · Maximum six participants · Selection required
journeys.j1_desc: A cultural and geographic expedition from the Pacific coast through the high Andes — Paracas, Nazca, Arequipa, Titicaca, Palcoyo, Machu Picchu and Cusco — with ritual integration embedded along the route.
journeys.j2_desc: A structured field-based immersion deep in the Peruvian Amazon forest. River transfer from Pucallpa into remote basin territory, alternating cycles of guided traditional practice and integration.

guide.title: Marcello Buglione
guide.body1: With a foundation in strategic communication, NLP and hypnosis, and decades of international training, Marcello is more than a guide. He is the architect of the experience.
guide.body2: His evolution into immersive Peruvian journeys distils complex cultural wisdom into precise, transformative travel paths for executives, entrepreneurs and professionals operating at high altitudes of life.
guide.quote: We do not design entertainment. We design attention, presence, and experience.

hero.title: The Andean Arc
hero.desc: A private cultural expedition from the Sacred Valley through the high Andes, the Amazon and the Pacific coast — twenty-one days, six participants, one curated path.

premise.lead: Five chapters. Twenty-one days. Six participants. One curated path.
premise.p1: The Andean Arc is not a circuit of sights. It is a sequenced journey designed for depth — beginning in the Sacred Valley, rising into the high Andes, descending into the Amazon and closing on the Pacific coast.
premise.p2: Ritual is woven into the route, not sold as an addition. Hospitality is selected from boutique and heritage properties chosen for atmosphere, not for brand recognition.

i1.label: Cusco
i1.desc: Arrival, private welcome, acclimatisation. Restored colonial residence in the historic quarter.

i2.label: Pisac
i2.desc: Ancient market and Inca citadel. Ofrenda alla Pachamama — a quiet offering to the land before the journey begins.

i3.label: Ollantaytambo
i3.desc: One of the most intact Inca urban centres. Private guided interpretation at dawn.

i4.label: Machu Picchu
i4.desc: Arrival via the Belmond Hiram Bingham train. Early-access entry — the first to enter, before the valley opens to the wider world.

i1.label: Preparation
i1.desc: Preparatory fasting and setting of intention. Private briefing with the practitioner.

i2.label: Private Ayahuasca Ceremony
i2.desc: Held in a private maloca with a trusted local practitioner. Structured, protected, unhurried.

i3.label: Kinsa Cocha
i3.desc: Three sacred lagoons at altitude — a day of integration and silence in the high landscape.

i4.label: Wachuma / San Pedro
i4.desc: A daytime ceremony with a Lesley Myburg. The medicine of the Andes, in its native terrain.

i1.label: Humantay Lake
i1.desc: Pre-dawn departure. A glacial lake at 4,200m — turquoise, improbable, silent.

i2.label: Palcoyo
i2.desc: The less-trafficked rainbow mountain — chosen for solitude over spectacle.

i3.label: Mountain Lodge
i3.desc: Nights in lodge properties immersed in the Andean landscape. Rest, altitude, open sky.

i1.label: Lake Titicaca
i1.desc: Premium lakeside lodge. Private vessel on the highest navigable lake in the world.

i2.label: Colca Canyon
i2.desc: One of the deepest canyons on Earth. Dawn observation of Andean condors in thermal flight.

i3.label: Arequipa
i3.desc: The white colonial city against El Misti volcano. Boutique heritage residence, private gastronomic evening.

i1.label: Nazca
i1.desc: Early-morning private flight over the Nazca Lines.

i2.label: Ica
i2.desc: Boutique desert hacienda. Private Pisco tasting in a working bodega. Dunes at golden hour.

i3.label: Paracas
i3.desc: Pacific desert reserve. Ballestas Islands wildlife. Paragliding. The ocean after three weeks in the mountains.

i4.label: Lima
i4.desc: Closing dinner in Lima - Barranco. Private transfer and departure.

ritual.title: Embedded, not advertised.
ritual.desc: Three ritual moments are woven into the journey itself. They are guided by Marcello with trusted local practitioners, held in safe and prepared environments.

i1.title: Pachamama Offering
i1.desc: An arrival ceremony — a quiet offering to the land before the journey begins.

i2.title: Ayahuasca Ceremony
i2.desc: Held in La Pacha Temple under the guidance of Master Nacho Rodriguez in a structured and protected setting.

i3.title: Wachuma (San Pedro)
i3.desc: A daytime ceremony with a local facilitator, in a safe and prepared environment.

closing.title: The Andean Arc opens to six participants per departure.

amazon.hero_title: There's a point in life where understanding is no longer enough. You have to cross through.
amazon.hero_desc: A 22-day Amazonian retreat at San Alejandro, guided by Maestro Carlos "Chichi" Escudero. This is not a vacation. It is not a cure. It is a serious commitment, with an equally serious preparation, for those who feel something in their life needs to change at a deep level.
amazon.hero_img_alt: Amazon rainforest canopy at San Alejandro, Peruvian Amazon
amazon.premise_lead: Twenty-two days. One continuous, deep Amazonian immersion at San Alejandro.
amazon.premise_body1: Hosted at San Alejandro, in the heart of the Peruvian Amazon, this retreat offers participants the opportunity to work with traditional master plants in a context deeply connected to the living traditions of Amazonian medicine. From Pucallpa, we travel upriver to the San Alejandro region, where a selected lodge and village setting become the base for a continuous Master Plant Dieta guided by Maestro Carlos "Chichi" Escudero.
amazon.premise_body2: Arrival in Pucallpa is set for November 1, 2026. The retreat program runs from November 3 to 24, 2026, with departure on November 25, 2026. Selection is rigorous. Preparation is mandatory. The retreat is not available without both.
amazon.qualify_intro: The people who arrive at San Alejandro are often going through a deep transformation: a crisis, a loss, burnout, a question they can no longer postpone. They are people willing to commit seriously, open to learning and discipline, who feel an authentic calling toward this path — not simple curiosity.
amazon.qualify_no_label: This path might not be right for you if
amazon.qualify_no1: You're looking for a quick fix to your problems.
amazon.qualify_no3: You're not willing to follow a three-month preparation protocol.
amazon.qualify_no4: You're looking for a spiritual vacation.
amazon.qualify_no5: You're not willing to question deep-seated beliefs about yourself.
amazon.qualify_no6: You don't have real availability for the preparatory work before the retreat.
amazon.qualify_yes_label: This path might be right for you if
amazon.qualify_yes1: You're going through a significant transformation in your life.
amazon.qualify_yes2: You're willing to commit seriously to the process, from start to finish.
amazon.qualify_yes3: You're open to the learning and discipline the Dieta requires.
amazon.qualify_yes4: You feel an authentic calling toward this path, not just curiosity.
amazon.qualify_clarity: We don't write this to discourage you, but for clarity. An honest application — even one that leads to "not now" — is worth more than a sign-up made for the wrong reasons.
amazon.why_title: Why I return to San Alejandro.
amazon.why_subtitle:
There are places you visit.
And places that become part of your life.
amazon.why_p1: I met Maestro Carlos "Chichi" Escudero almost ten years ago. Since then I have brought people here from all over the world, returning several times a year to work with him and with the living traditions of the Amazon forest.
amazon.why_p2: Over the years, San Alejandro has become far more than a destination. It has become a place I know intimately: the river, the forest, the trails, the local communities, the plants, the silences and the rhythms that shape daily life.
amazon.why_p3: I have lived some of the most significant moments of my life here.
amazon.why_p4: I remember the long boat journeys along the river. The days spent in the forest searching for plants. The conversations around the fire. The laughter shared over meals. Sunset fishing. Friendships born between people who arrived from different continents, united by the same inner search.
amazon.why_p5: For many years I called San Alejandro my center of transformation.
amazon.why_p7: But because here I have seen something happen that is increasingly rare to find today: authenticity, humanity and a genuine relationship with the medicine of the forest.
amazon.why_p8: After a long period away from the Amazon, I chose to return here.
amazon.why_p9: Not because it is the most famous place.
amazon.why_p10: Not because it is the most luxurious.
amazon.why_p11: Nor because it is the easiest to reach.
amazon.why_p12: I return because I know the people. I know the place. I know the work that is done.
amazon.why_p13: And above all because, when I bring someone into such an important journey, I want to be able to say with sincerity:
amazon.who_title: There isn't just one reason to come.
amazon.who_subtitle: But there is almost always a turning point.
amazon.who1_title: A crisis that can no longer be postponed
amazon.who1_desc: A marriage that ended, a diagnosis, a loss, a question about who you've become. Something that broke the autopilot and demands a real answer.
amazon.who2_desc: Executives, entrepreneurs, professionals who have built a great deal externally and feel they have lost touch with something essential within.
amazon.who3_desc: A change of phase — turning fifty, a divorce, children leaving home, a career coming to a close — that asks to be gone through, not just managed.
amazon.who4_desc: Not surface-level curiosity, but a question carried inside for years that, at a certain point, asks for a concrete step.
amazon.arc1_desc: November 1, 2026. Decompression at a selected hotel in Pucallpa. Briefing, medical checks, equipment review.
amazon.arc2_desc: Private boat transfer from Pucallpa to San Alejandro, in the Peruvian Amazon. The journey itself is part of the immersion.
amazon.arc3_desc: Remote lodge and village setting at San Alejandro. The pace of life slows down. Daylight, river, fire.
amazon.arc4_desc: November 3–24, 2026. Structured cycles of guided traditional practice with Maestro Chichi, alternated with full integration days.
amazon.arc5_desc: Return journey along the river, an integration day in Pucallpa, departure on November 25, 2026.
amazon.maloca_title: The Maloca: the heart of the journey
amazon.maloca_desc: This is where the ceremonies come alive. The maloca is the temple of our transformation, where the circle closes and healing begins.
amazon.maloca_img_alt: Interior of the ceremonial maloca at San Alejandro, circle of participants during a ceremony
amazon.prepe_subtitle: It isn't the twenty-two days that make the difference...
amazon.prepe_p2: The Master Plant Dieta does not begin on the day of arrival in Pucallpa. It begins three months earlier, the moment a participant agrees to abstain from alcohol and substances, to discipline their diet, and to slow the mental and emotional rhythms that daily life imposes.
amazon.prepe_p3: This is not an organizational detail. It is the very condition that makes the work with the plants safe, deep and truly transformative.
amazon.prepe_p4: An unprepared body and mind meet the forest's medicine only on the surface. A prepared body and mind, instead, can receive it fully: with the clarity needed to move through the ceremonies, the stability needed to hold what emerges, and the capacity to truly integrate what is lived.
amazon.prepe_p5: This is why selection is rigorous and preparation mandatory. Not to make the path harder, but to protect its value. The master plants work with those who arrive ready to receive them.
amazon.prepe_closing: The quality of your preparation will determine the depth of your experience.
amazon.plants_desc: At the heart of this Amazonian retreat is the Master Plant Dieta, a traditional Amazonian practice in which participants work individually with specific plants under Maestro Chichi's guidance. Each plant carries its own traditional focus within Amazonian plant medicine.
amazon.plant1_focus: Protection, grounding and connection with the forest.
amazon.plant2_focus: Emotional opening, compassion and heart-centered work.
amazon.plants_note: The specific plants used during the retreat may vary based on Maestro Chichi's guidance and participants' individual needs.
amazon.plants_honesty: It must be said clearly: working with the master plants, and Ayahuasca in particular, can bring moments of real emotional discomfort during the ceremonies — fear, pain, direct confrontation with what has been avoided for years. This is not a side effect to hide. It is part of the process, and is one of the reasons why preparation and Maestro Chichi's guidance are non-negotiable conditions.
amazon.plants_cta: Download the Free Guide to the Master Plants →
amazon.location_p1: Hosted at San Alejandro, in the heart of the Peruvian Amazon, this immersive retreat offers participants the opportunity to work with traditional master plants in a context deeply connected to the living traditions of Amazonian medicine.
amazon.location_p2: Reached by private river transfer from Pucallpa, San Alejandro offers the remote, undisturbed environment required by a traditional Master Plant Dieta: a place shaped by the forest, the river, and decades of practice with Amazonian plants.
amazon.location_q1: For many years I called San Alejandro my center of transformation.
amazon.location_q2: Here I have seen people change.
amazon.location_q3: Here I have built friendships that still last today.
amazon.location_q4: Here I learned that the medicine of the forest is not only about the plants, but also about the human relationships that form around them.
amazon.maestro_p1: This Amazonian retreat takes place in collaboration with Maestro Carlos "Chichi" Escudero, a traditional Amazonian healer and master plant practitioner with decades of experience within the living traditions of the Peruvian Amazon.
amazon.maestro_p2: Raised in the Amazon rainforest, Maestro Chichi's relationship with the master plants spans a lifetime of direct, ancestral knowledge, passed down through generations of practitioners in the region. His work is rooted in a deep and ongoing connection with the forest itself: its plants, its rhythms, and the traditional practices that surround them.
amazon.maestro_p3: Throughout the retreat, Maestro Chichi guides every cycle of the Master Plant Dieta, drawing on this long experience to keep traditional practices at the center of the program.
amazon.maestro_p4: I have known Chichi for almost ten years. Over this time I have brought people here from all over the world and had the privilege of working directly alongside him in hundreds of ceremonies. He is one of the few people I would trust without hesitation with someone I love.
amazon.maestro_img_alt: Maestro Carlos Chichi Escudero, traditional Amazonian healer
